How does the SCRIPE CRM v3.0 Suite Unify Managed Graph Canvases, 13 Routes, and AstraFlow Persistence?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE CRM v3.0 establishes end-to-end operational sovereignty across 13 core routes through a managed @xyflow/react v12 Workflow Studio, a modular @core/crud unified view engine, dynamic Jira-style Transition Screens, and an in-house .NET 10 AstraFlow 2.3.0 monolith anchored in PostgreSQL Single Source of Truth.1

  1. The 2D Workflow Studio v3.0 features 12 magnetic perimeter ports (ConnectionMode.Loose), a canonical __start__ origin node, Jira wildcard * ALL satellite stubs, and cycle-safe Dagre/ELK rank layout.2
  2. The @core/crud architecture unifies all 13 CRM routes (Leads, Deals, Accounts, Contacts, Activities) on GenericCrudView and virtualized GenericWorkflowKanban driven by dynamic stageKey.3
  3. A dynamic react-hook-form + zod Transition Screen executes a Smart 3-State Drop with full Deal 360 and Lead 360 progression parity, protecting against OWASP A01/A04 privilege escalation.4
  4. The backend .NET 10 UniversalWorkflowEngine enforces 3-tier Specific-Wins precedence (Exact A->B > Outbound A->* > Global *->B), rollback locks, and compile-time [AstraGenerateMapping].5

  1. Origin __start__ Anchor ↗

    Anchors the visual canvas top-left with an animated green pill and entry wire.

  2. Studio Canvas Container ↗

    Provides managed zoom, pan, background grid, and multi-selection canvas.

  3. 12-Port Loose Stage Nodes ↗

    Renders 3 discrete magnetic ports per face with ConnectionMode.Loose.

  4. Multi-Parallel Loose Edges ↗

    Connects stages with dynamic Euclidean port pairing and parallel transition support.

  5. Cycle-Safe Dagre & ELK ↗

    Breaks back-edge cycles to force terminal stages to the far right with generous ranksep.

  6. Stage Rule Catalog ↗

    Configures required exit fields, party verification, and deal conversion actions.

  7. High-Resolution Export ↗

    Serializes full canvas to high-density PNG with html-to-image.

The Workflow Studio replaces brittle, hardcoded custom SVG coordinate systems with @xyflow/react v12. Every pipeline stage operates as a custom reactive node featuring category pills (todo, in_progress, done, lost), SLA milestones, and an interactive * From Any inbound port. Transitions are modeled as Bezier curves with reconnection handles, while auto-layout algorithms calculate clean horizontal and vertical arrangements.2

The monolithic generic-crud-view.tsx is partitioned into focused, single-responsibility sub-components. GenericWorkflowKanban powers both Leads and Opportunities using a polymorphic contract constrained to records containing an id and stageKey. Rigid status enums are completely replaced by dynamic stageKey columns defined in the pipeline configuration, while @tanstack/react-virtual ensures 60 FPS scrolling across high-volume pipelines.3

How does the Smart 3-State Drop evaluate stage transitions and render dynamic forms?

Diagram structure
  • Sales Representative user
  • GenericWorkflowKanban kanban
  • WorkflowTransitionDialog dialog
  • UniversalWorkflowEngine engine
  • PostgreSQL CRM Database postgres
  • user → kanban · Drag Card from Stage A to Stage B
  • kanban → dialog · Intercept Drop & Open Transition Screen
  • dialog → user · Present Dynamic RHF + Zod Validation Form
  • user → dialog · Submit Close Notes & Outcome Fields
  • dialog → engine · POST /api/v1/crm/opportunities/{id}/stage
  • engine → postgres · UPDATE StageKey + INSERT StageHistory + Outbox
  • postgres → engine · Commit Transaction
  • engine → dialog · 200 OK Result<OpportunityResponse>
  • dialog → kanban · Close Dialog & Invalidate Query Cache
  1. Drag Card Across Columns ↗

    User picks up deal or lead card and hovers over target stage column.

  2. Smart 3-State Drop Evaluation ↗

    Kanban checks direct edges, gate requirements, and lock conditions.

  3. Dynamic Transition Screen ↗

    Dialog renders dynamic input fields derived from workflow exit rules.

  4. Backend Precedence Validation ↗

    UniversalWorkflowEngine verifies permissions, rollbacks, and exit criteria.

  5. Atomic PostgreSQL Persistence ↗

    Updates record stage, appends stage history log, and emits Outbox event.

When a card is dropped on a column, GenericWorkflowKanban executes a Smart 3-State Drop evaluation: Direct Allowed (no exit gates exist and the card advances immediately with an optimistic UI update), Transition Screen Required (the target stage or transition edge requires mandatory fields such as closeNotes, lossReasonCode, or validate.verified_party, prompting WorkflowTransitionDialog with dynamic react-hook-form and zod validation), or Disallowed / Blocked (the transition path is restricted or backward rollback is disallowed, rejecting the drop and displaying a diagnostic locked pill). Both Deal 360 and Lead 360 views enforce identical progression gates when advancing stages from header action buttons.4

Zero Client Privilege Escalation (OWASP A01 / A04)

To prevent privilege escalation attacks where untrusted clients submit reserved evaluation keys inside CustomFields, the backend sanitization pipeline strips keys such as userRoles, approvedByRoles, visitedStageKeys, hasManagerApproval, and ActorUserId before exit checklist and rule evaluation occurs.1

How does the .NET 10 UniversalWorkflowEngine enforce Specific-Wins precedence and transactional persistence?

The backend .NET 10 UniversalWorkflowEngine enforces deterministic graph evaluation with Specific-Wins Precedence. The inverted rollback lock bug is resolved by ensuring if (isBackward && !matched.AllowRollback) restricts only backward transitions while permitting unrestricted forward flows. Furthermore, all stages (including done and lost) can declare outbound transitions, enabling seamless Reopen (Closed Lost -> Discovery) and Requalification (Disqualified -> Working) operations.5

Precedence TierTransition Matching LogicEvaluation OrderResult Contract
Tier 1: Exact Direct EdgeCurrentStageKey -> TargetStageKey1st Priority (Specific-Wins)Direct transition rules apply
Tier 2: Outbound WildcardCurrentStageKey -> *2nd PriorityStage-specific exit rules apply
Tier 3: Global Inbound* -> TargetStageKey or AllowInboundFromAny3rd PriorityGlobal transition rules apply
Tier 4: Fallback BlockedNo matching edge or wildcard transitionTerminal EvaluationResult.Failure(CrmErrors.Workflow)

Unified commands MoveOpportunityStageCommand and MoveLeadStageCommand persist stage mutations atomically to PostgreSQL. Legacy terminal endpoints are unified under stage evaluation, recording complete audit history and dispatching transactional Outbox events.6
